newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's SNI has $44.3 mln profit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's SNI has $44.3 mln profit in 1996.

text.p: Morocco's private conglomerate Societe Nationale d'Investissement made a consolidated net profit of 417 million dirhams ($44.3 million) in 1996, up 10.3 percent over 1995, the group said on Wednesday.
M'Fadel Lahlou, chairman of the conglomerate, told Reuters that SNI, one of the stock market's most liquid stocks, increased transactions turnover in 1996 by 30.9 percent to 2.0 billion dirhams.
Total turnover rose 16 percent to 4.4 billion dirhams in 1996, from 3.8 billion dirhams in 1995, Lahlou said. The results were released after a meeting of the SNI board of directors on Monday.
With diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, SNI agro-industry turnover rose 34 percent to 1.5 billion dirhams while the construction sector jumped 37 percent to 1.6 billion dirhams in 1996.

Mines and chemicals turnover grew 11 percent to 498 million dirhams, finance and brokerage rose seven million dirhams to 282 million dirhams and the net debt ratio (debt/shareholder equity) remained at 38 percent.
SNI said it would pay a dividend of 12 dirhams in 1996, compared with 10 in 1995.
Morocco's second largest private holding, SNI company has a capital of 990 million dirhams and a market capitalisation of more than 7.0 billion dirhams.
One of the 47 stocks listed on the Casablanca stock exchange, SNI was last traded at 735 dirhams.
